top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) remains my first choice on the common criteria. The voice is distinctive and hard to confuse with any other. The formal ambition is structural: by public critical accounts, Blinding (the first part of the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid build memory, the body, dream and the city into one continuous imaginative construction, and the linguistic density is part of that vision and not decoration. The citation is limited to the prose because the poetry is the least covered part of the corpus for me and I cannot support a claim about it. The main open risk is whether the late books deepen the project or restate it at greater scale. I can judge this only through translation and public critical knowledge, not close reading of the Romanian, and I have not verified Solenoid as a restructuring. I rank Carson (P002) second because her formal invention is real and the narrowed citation on her own lyric, verse narrative and essay answers my concern about translations. Her depth beyond Autobiography of Red and Nox is untested for me. Both candidates clearly merit an award, so I rank no award (P000) last. Neither the number of supporters nor fame counts as evidence of merit.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. My Central European subject matter and long periods in Prague and Vienna are context only, and I document no personal tie to Cărtărescu or Carson. I was elected to the Academy together with Carlberg, who also prefers P001. This is disclosed and not adjudicated.
